dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The transactions have May effective dates but 31 May posting dates"
"Dealer import batches passed row-count and reconciliation controls"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31 May cluster is consistent with the contracted dealer-file submission process."
"The annual-plan transactions have May effective dates but were posted at month-end."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The supplied evidence does not independently prove the underlying customer payments or dealer-origin records."
"Bank/payment records or original dealer transaction records would change the judgment if they revealed duplicate payments, nonexistent transactions, or reconciliation discrepancies."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "perform a sample reconciliation against dealer source/payment records"
"Escalate only if that validation finds discrepancies."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not alter the May revenue or pipeline. Label the 31 May items as contractual month-end postings in the trend pack"
"No material issue; do not escalate as duplicate revenue, manipulation, or a pipeline defect."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Source transaction IDs are unique, so the cluster is not explained by duplicate source events" is useful evidence but does not independently rule out duplicate underlying customer payments or dealer-origin records.

"The email confirms that dealers are permitted to submit annual-renewal files monthly" may overstate an email as proof of contractual permission; it should be treated as corroboration unless the contracts themselves were reviewed.

"Manipulated reporting — rejected" is stronger than the evidence supports; the effective/posting-date distinction and import reconciliation reduce concern but do not fully exclude manipulation outside the tested controls.
"Do not alter the May revenue or pipeline" is broader than the demonstrated evidence, particularly because the submission does not specify what pipeline controls or downstream analytics were tested.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately retained the possibility of duplicate payments, nonexistent transactions, or dealer-record discrepancies, but did not fully test the strongest alternative: the import may reconcile internally while underlying dealer or payment records contain duplicates or omissions. A second important alternative—that the event-time fields distort downstream retention or cohort analytics despite correct accounting—was largely missed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide reproducible, granular evidence: identify the two West dealers and relevant cohorts, show the posted_at versus effective_event_date distribution, report unique source_event_id counts and reconciliation differences by batch, and explicitly require downstream analytics to use effective_event_date.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South tickets fell from 793 before the pilot to 191 after it, but the other non-pilot regions show a very similar proportional decline over the same period"
"NOVA-S1 has 90 transferred sessions versus 932 under LEGACY, but also 591 abandoned and 507 error sessions"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The IVR data also weaken the positive interpretation: NOVA-S1 has far fewer transfers but substantially more abandoned/error sessions, and sessions ending before authentication are excluded from CareDesk case reporting."
"A before/after decline alone cannot establish causality because of concurrent regional changes and excluded IVR sessions."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Lower agent transfers may indicate greater self-service containment, but the abandonment/error volume makes that interpretation uncertain."

"Unknowns: How many customers actually resolved their issue successfully through NovaIVR... Whether customers who disappeared from CareDesk reporting subsequently contacted support through another channel."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."

"Keep the South pilot running, but do not expand nationally yet. Recompute outcomes using all IVR sessions—including pre-authentication abandonment/errors—and compare South against non-pilot regions with matched time windows and service-event controls."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Facts vs inferences vs causal claims vs unknowns"
"What customer-outcome metric besides CareDesk case count and agent transfers shows that NovaIVR improved customer experience, and how does South compare with the non-pilot regions on that metric?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The claim that "the other non-pilot regions show a very similar proportional decline" is not accompanied by specific regional counts, dates, rows, or a calculation, making the comparison difficult to reproduce.
"Farah explicitly confirms this reporting limitation" is asserted without quoting the relevant email passage or identifying the specific metric definition.
"Service events occurred in the South during the relevant period" is only assigned medium confidence and is not linked to particular events, dates, or observed complaint changes.

Recomputing outcomes using "all IVR sessions" is directionally appropriate, but abandonment and error sessions are not themselves customer complaints or failed resolutions; they require linked journey outcomes or sampled-call validation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles the strongest adverse interpretation well: the ticket decline may be a capture or routing failure caused by pre-authentication IVR abandonment and errors rather than an experience improvement. It also considers common non-pilot-region changes and service events. It could more explicitly preserve the benign alternative that some abandoned or non-case-producing sessions may nevertheless reflect resolved or non-complaint contacts, so abandonment alone cannot quantify harm.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible regional time-series comparison around the 10 May rollout, then link IVR sessions to downstream resolution, repeat contacts, and sampled call outcomes; this would test both the capture-failure mechanism and the possibility that abandonment represents non-complaint or successfully resolved journeys.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `inverter_events.csv` for all four events being `cleared=yes` and `impact_mw=0`.
It cites `inverter_events.csv` for the 1–7 minute duration range and the May 29 to June 4 timestamp change.
The wording distinguishes evidence from inference: “This is a data-scope check, not evidence of equipment failure.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the equipment-failure hypothesis against multiple fields: zero impact, cleared status, short duration, and lack of other direct failure evidence.
It appropriately states that event wording alone is insufficient and proposes a timestamp/scope check rather than constructing a failure narrative.
The analysis relies primarily on one source file rather than triangulating an independent operational or communications channel.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Confidence is high for directly observed file contents but the timestamp issue is limited to a “cheap timestamp check.”
The conclusion is explicitly conditional: “stop unless it reveals an export-boundary error.”
The submission does not claim that the file proves broader plant health; it limits the conclusion to the listed events and available evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommended action—verify whether the file is intended to span both dates—is low-cost and directly discriminates between a legitimate date transition and an export-boundary problem.
“Perform the one cheap timestamp/scope check, then stop” is proportionate to zero MW impact, cleared events, and short durations.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the supplied evidence: four cleared events, zero MW impact, and durations of only 1–7 minutes.
It avoids inventing a plant problem from the event wording and preserves a narrowly scoped data-quality check.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claim is present. “No material anomaly identified” is appropriately scoped to the four records in `inverter_events.csv`, though it should not be read as a claim about plant conditions outside that file.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The May 29-to-June 4 transition may be an ordinary date boundary or a legitimate multi-day export rather than an error; the proposed scope check appropriately tests this without treating it as evidence of equipment failure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State explicitly that no independent telemetry, communications log, or event-detail source was reviewed, and that the stop recommendation applies to this export rather than proving the absence of all possible plant issues.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` for the 28 May and 29 May DSM totals and shows the arithmetic for the 31.6% reduction: “The 31.6% DSM-penalty reduction is arithmetically reproducible.”
It cites `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md` and `dispatch_blocks.csv` for the mismatch in reported and block-level MWh totals.

It identifies that 29 May contains 12 `pilot_revision` blocks and that the remainder uses `qca_base`, but it does not cite or calculate the actual same-day base-versus-submitted schedule counterfactual.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly recognizes that the comparison uses different days: “this is only a one-day comparison against a different day; weather, wind conditions, operating conditions, schedule mix and other confounders are not controlled.”
It lists plausible alternative explanations, but largely only states them rather than testing them against the available same-day `qca_base` and `pilot_revision` blocks.
It uses the commercial extract to note settlement mechanics, but does not triangulate those mechanics with a same-day penalty or deviation analysis.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission appropriately distinguishes observation from causation: “The strongest defensible claim is therefore: the observed penalty was 31.6% lower on the AI-assisted day than on the selected conventional comparison day. It is not proof of a causal pilot impact.”
It identifies important unknowns, including comparability of wind/stow conditions, the impact-note reconciliation issue, and whether repeated events would replicate the result.
Calibration is incomplete because it does not quantify or discuss the smaller same-day benefit that can be estimated from the 29 May base-versus-submitted schedules.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation “Continue the pilot and use it for controlled evaluation, but do not claim a causal 31.6% saving or expand nationally yet” is proportionate and preserves potential operational value.
The proposed next measurement—multiple comparable high-wind/stow events with pre-specified accepted schedules, meter generation, weather/stow conditions and DSM settlement—is sensible.
The action would be more discriminating if it first required the available 29 May same-day counterfactual analysis before relying primarily on future events.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly rejects treating the 31.6% different-day comparison as a causal estimate and correctly retains a nonzero possibility of pilot value by recommending continued controlled evaluation.

However, it misses a central qualification required by the evidence: compare `base_schedule_mw` with `submitted_schedule_mw` on 29 May to estimate the pilot-day same-day effect, which is smaller than the 31.6% headline rather than no value.
Thus the conclusion is directionally sound but under-scoped relative to the strongest available analysis.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the impact note's 4,455.2 / 4,231.1 MWh figures “do not reconcile” is presented as high-confidence, but the submission does not show the exact aggregation, units, block range, or timestamp basis needed to verify the discrepancy.

The largest analytical omission is not an unsupported claim but an unperformed central test: the submission does not calculate the 29 May same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`.

The claim that the selected comparison day is not sufficiently comparable is appropriately framed as unknown, not established; the submission should avoid implying that the comparison is invalid without checking available weather, wind, stow, and operating data.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction is not a causal estimate because it compares different days, but the pilot may still have produced a smaller same-day improvement on 29 May. The appropriate interpretation is therefore “possible operational value, with the headline effect overstated by the day-level comparison,” rather than either “31.6% proven savings” or “no pilot value.”
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compute and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual: compare DSM settlement outcomes and deviations under `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` for the pilot-revision blocks, then reconcile that result with accepted schedules, meter generation, and the impact-note aggregation basis.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The declaration for P1001 uses tariff code 90211000" — `declaration.pdf`
"Switzerland's approved code for P1001 is 90211000 effective 2025-01-01" — `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx` — Swiss Matrix
"The automated flag identifies a mismatch to Helios 90211090" — `review_note.txt`

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Likely declaration coding error — rejected: the Swiss country-specific reference independently supports the declared 90211000."
"Product-master mismatch proves an incorrect declaration — rejected: the product master contains the Helios commercial code, while the Swiss matrix uses a jurisdiction-specific local code."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Missing Evidence"
"A Swiss Tares/ruling or product-specific customs decision confirming the legally applicable classification for P1001 on 2025-11-04."
"The Swiss matrix itself says its working classification should be confirmed against Tares/ruling for legal use."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Switzerland's tariff matrix explicitly approves 90211000 effective 2025-01-01."
"The tariff matrix states that Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code and matching strings across jurisdictions are not expected"
"The automated comparison is therefore comparing codes from different jurisdictional code systems."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Perform one targeted check against the Swiss Tares/ruling record for P1001 and the declaration date."
"Do not amend or escalate the declaration solely because 90211000 differs from Helios 90211090."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "explicitly approves" could be read as establishing legal classification conclusively, although the submission appropriately limits this by stating that Tares/ruling confirmation is still required for legal use.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211000 could still be an incorrect Swiss classification despite the jurisdictional code-system explanation; a product-specific Swiss Tares/ruling or customs decision for P1001 on the declaration date would be needed to distinguish that possibility.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add exact sheet names, row or cell references, and quoted source text for the Swiss matrix and Read Me entries, while preserving the targeted Tares/ruling check before treating the classification as legally confirmed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 claims preference = Yes and declares origin as United States" — `declaration.pdf`
"SUP-02/P1006 has a supplier-origin record for Ireland, but its validity ended 31 Jul 2025 and the register marks it “Expired”" — `supplier_origin_register.csv`
"No current document reference was found for SUP-02/P1006 on 18 Sep 2025" — `supplier_declaration_reference.txt` / register search result

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference = Yes proves entitlement’ — rejected: the declaration records the claim but does not establish the underlying preferential-origin qualification."
"‘Current ERP/manufacturing origin is enough’ — rejected: the workshop explicitly distinguishes ordinary COO from evidence required to clear a preference claim."

"‘No register record proves no supplier evidence exists’ — rejected: the supplier-reference note itself states that absence from the register does not prove that the document does not exist elsewhere."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Do not treat the Irish preferential-origin claim as supported yet."
"the available evidence does not establish that P1006 qualifies for preferential origin on 18 Sep 2025"
"No current document reference was found" and "absence from the register does not prove that the document does not exist elsewhere."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "the workshop explicitly states that ERP/COO data are not sufficient to clear a preference claim."
"The commercial invoice also states United States as the manufacturing country" — `commercial_invoice.pdf`
"The applicable preference agreement/rule and product-specific origin test used to support the claim" is listed as missing evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold/verify the preference claim before relying on the 0% duty treatment."
"Request and validate the supplier declaration and applicable origin rule for P1006 covering the declaration date."
"Until validated, do not rely on the preference claim or release it as supported solely from the current packet."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission assigns "High" confidence to "No current document reference was found for SUP-02/P1006 on 18 Sep 2025," but does not quote the actual search result, search scope, or search timestamp; the claim is therefore traceable but not fully independently auditable from the submission alone.

The statement that the register shows the record as expired is appropriately limited as evidence against relying on the claim, but expiry in the register alone does not establish that no valid supplier declaration or other qualifying evidence existed elsewhere.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Irish preferential-origin claim may still be valid: the expired register entry and United States manufacturing-country statement do not by themselves disprove preferential origin, and a current supplier declaration plus the applicable product-specific origin rule could establish qualification despite the register status.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the exact register row, search result, supplier-reference text, and applicable preference rule, then explicitly test the product-specific origin criteria against the documented supply route and qualifying processing.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “SOP defines the routine target as 24 hours from required evidence available to disposition” — cites qc_release_sop.md and identifies the relevant clock definition.
“batch_release.csv contains receipt_ts, lab_complete_ts, and qcore_release_ts, but no required-evidence-available timestamp” — cites a specific file and fields.
“LabTrack's snapshot is dated 29 Jul 23:00 and is described as a 48-hour analytics extract” — cites source_freshness.csv and acknowledges source limitations.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “Receipt-to-release is an adequate substitute” — rejected because receipt can precede completion of required evidence.

“The extract does not contain the SOP-defined start point” — correctly identifies a measurement-definition problem, but does not test whether qcore_release_ts is an interface commit rather than a decision time or examine its hourly concentration.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “cannot be treated as the official 24-hour routine service metric” — appropriately limits the conclusion to KPI use rather than claiming a proven operational delay.
“If these checks reconcile the timestamps, the apparent cycle time could be used” — makes the decision conditional on validation and recognizes missing evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Verify before using the apparent cycle time as a KPI” — appropriately reframes the issue from optimizing an apparent delay to validating the metric.

“The smallest useful check is to obtain the evidence-availability timestamp and confirm the timestamp definition/time zone used by QCore” — proposes a focused and reversible validation step, though it omits profiling the release timestamp and checking event-versus-interface timing.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “The apparent 1.5-day cycle is the official QC KPI” — rejected using the SOP clock definition.

“Receipt-to-release is an adequate substitute” — rejected with a plausible operational rationale, but the submission does not test the strongest competing explanation that the delay is caused by interface timing or asynchronous extracts.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “A validated required_evidence_available_ts field” and “confirmation from the data catalog that the QCore timestamps use the correct definition and timezone” — requests relevant, decision-linked evidence.

The request is prioritized, but it should also ask for an event log or decision timestamp and source snapshot identifiers to distinguish workflow delay from interface timing and temporal inconsistency.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The apparent 1.5-day cycle” is not supported by a cited calculation, row, or distribution in the submission.

The recommendation that the smallest useful check is only the evidence-availability timestamp and timezone is incomplete: timestamp event semantics, hourly release-time profiling, and snapshot alignment are also material to KPI validity.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent cycle time may primarily reflect QCore interface-commit timing or asynchronous source extracts rather than the duration of the QC decision workflow. The reported release timestamps should therefore be profiled by hour and reconciled to an event or decision log before operational action is taken.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and analyze a reconciled event-level extract containing required-evidence-available, disposition/decision, and QCore interface-commit timestamps, with timezone and source-snapshot metadata; first profile qcore_release_ts by hour to test for the suspected batch concentration.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Multiple open requests have exact manufacturer-part-number, revision and UOM matches at other sites"
"Some exact matches have sufficient available stock and no critical reservation, e.g. HA-0026 for PR-260701 and ME-0017 for PR-260710"
"Global availability can lag local reservations" — `maintenance_email.txt` + `source_freshness.csv`
"Exact MPN/revision/UOM; not critical-reserved; qualified common" for PR-260701 and similar row-level classifications.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "There is a real spare-parts reuse opportunity, but the sample should be split into ‘actionable now’ and ‘engineering check’"
"Description-only matches should remain candidates until engineering confirms equivalence"
"Global available quantity alone proves transferable stock — rejected"
"Different descriptions mean different parts — rejected: ... manufacturer part number identifies the same item."

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Description-only/approximate requests can identify candidates but do not establish technical equivalence"
"I would not use raw global availability without checking reservations"
"A live stock/CMMS snapshot, because the supplied source data are snapshots and global availability may lag local reservations."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Exact manufacturer-part-number/revision/UOM matches with available, non-reserved stock provide the strongest evidence"
"Description-only matches should remain candidates until engineering confirms equivalence"
"Transfer approval would convert a candidate from ‘needs engineering check’ to actionable now only after those checks pass."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "‘Every semantic match is transferable’ — rejected"
"‘Global available quantity alone proves transferable stock’ — rejected"
"‘Different descriptions mean different parts’ — rejected"

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Current local reservation status for candidate stock"
"Engineering confirmation of manufacturer part number, revision/configuration and UOM for description-only matches"
"Confirmation that the receiving site is qualified for the candidate part"
"A live stock/CMMS snapshot"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The label "Actionable now" for exact matches may be too strong because the submission also acknowledges that the supplied availability and reservation data are snapshots and that global availability can lag local reservations; these should more safely be labeled conditionally actionable pending live confirmation.

"Exact MPN/revision/UOM; not critical-reserved; qualified common" is presented as established for each listed candidate, but the submission does not provide row-level values or clarify whether qualification and reservation checks are current.
The claim that transfer approval alone converts a candidate to "actionable now" omits possible logistics, receiving-site authorization, condition/inspection, and other transfer constraints.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The exact matches demonstrate high-confidence candidate value but not necessarily immediately actionable transfer value: stale or temporally inconsistent stock, reservations, qualification status, or local operating constraints could make even exact matches unavailable until a live CMMS and transfer-authorization check is completed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace "actionable now" with a conditional status and run one live, point-in-time validation for the highest-value exact match: confirm physical on-hand quantity, reservation/criticality, qualification, revision/UOM, and receiving-site authorization together before authorizing transfer.
